decisions.reason: Uses contrast-probe.txt: file-trace own RPC reads the same file (rules out disk, path, permission, workspace-scope) while the documentpreview tab via the api-workspace-files Remote fails with meta.status stuck at none; localizes the fault to the workspace-files resource-provider/RPC metadata chain, notes the host row is already declared, and does not blame the renderer or disk.

Treats the 62/62 per-module sweep and the single-module combo as the valid static-serving measurement and the ~4KB all-joined 404 as an artifact of exceeding the combo URL limit, explicitly rejecting it as missing-modules evidence; explains the real loader fetches per manifest url entries, matching the bounded-partitioning fact without citing a memorized constant.

Separates the paste-input fold warnings as an unrelated independent bug family; uses boot-manifest-excerpt.txt to explain the textpreview-to-documentpreview rename and the session-only canOpen scope causing the absolute-address claim failure, while correctly stating that scope change does not explain the stalled session-tab metadata.

Gives restart once first, then rollback to the verified published 0.1.3-alpha.2 escape hatch from discussion-excerpt.txt, then upstream follow-up to #5999 round 2; explicitly rejects plugin-side rewrite/retry/fallback workarounds and cites the alpha.1 roster mismatch as prior art, not proof of currently missing bytes.

Packages version/upgrade history, boot manifest, valid per-module sweep with the invalid-join caveat, same-file contrast with meta.status, console excerpt and host-side notes; proposes concrete boot diagnostics: a real metadata read round-trip probe per declared resource service and resource-provider/Remote resolve-chain validation that would fail loud.

caps.reason: The report affirmatively concludes modules are served (62/62) and explicitly labels the joined-URL 404 as an oversized-URL artifact that must not be cited as missing modules.
The report explicitly rejects plugin-side rewrite/retry/fallback as a cure for the host-chain gap and proposes no duplicate service insertion.
